correctness.rationale: For all connected complete multipartite graphs, the proof is valid: every white vertex in V_i sees red/blue precisely outside V_i; a selected induced subgraph has no isolated vertex exactly when its support meets >=2 parts. A two-vertex DST solution forces two singleton parts; the remaining nonstar minimum is 3 when any part has size <=2 and 4 otherwise, by the stated constructions and singleton-color lower bound. For TDS, each color needs vertices in >=2 parts, so >=4 is necessary; explicit four-vertex constructions exist precisely for nonstars of order >=4. Stars require all vertices for DST and cannot have both TDS colors with edges; K_2 and K_3 are correctly handled. Exact, independent profile-occupancy enumeration on all 128 unordered profiles through N=10 and independent 177534 red/blue/white assignments across 58 profiles through N=8 matched the classification and the equivalence with prior 2-rainbow feasibility; bounded tests are corroboration only.
residual_risks: No finite enumeration certifies the infinite theorem; the independent neighborhood-based proof supplies that step.

Restrict to labels empty/red/blue (no double-color label), require both colors nonempty, and impose elementary support-in-at-least-two-parts conditions; this gives exactly DST and TDS feasibility and the target minima by trivial cardinality casework. The prior 2026 source defining the two total parameters additionally settles star, biclique, complete graph and general TDS bounds. Different title and unprinted corollary do not establish novelty.
